import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Parshin's conjecture

Parshin's conjecture (also called the Beilinson–Parshin conjecture) states that for any smooth
projective variety $X$ over a finite field, the higher algebraic $K$-groups of $X$ vanish up to
torsion, i.e. $K_i(X) \otimes \mathbb{Q} = 0$ for all $i > 0$.

Mathlib has no definition of higher algebraic $K$-theory. This file defines the $K$-groups
$K_n(X)$ of a scheme $X$ using Grayson's presentation of the $K$-groups of an exact category
by bounded acyclic binary multicomplexes [Gra2012]. For any exact category $\mathcal{N}$,
Grayson proves that Quillen's $K_n(\mathcal{N})$ is the quotient of the Grothendieck group
$K_0((B^q)^n \mathcal{N})$ of the exact category of $n$-dimensional bounded acyclic binary
multicomplexes in $\mathcal{N}$ by the subgroup generated by the classes of the multicomplexes
whose top and bottom differentials agree in at least one direction. We apply this to the exact
category of vector bundles (locally free $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules of finite rank) on $X$, which
gives the algebraic $K$-theory of $X$ in the sense of Quillen.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia, Parshin's conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parshin%27s_conjecture)
* [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
* [Gra2012] D. R. Grayson, *Algebraic K-theory via binary complexes*,
  J. Amer. Math. Soc. 25 (2012), 1149–1167.
  [doi:10.1090/S0894-0347-2012-00743-7](https://doi.org/10.1090/S0894-0347-2012-00743-7)
* [Kah2005] B. Kahn, *Algebraic K-theory, algebraic cycles and arithmetic geometry*,
  Handbook of K-theory I, Springer (2005).
-/

namespace ParshinsConjecture

open CategoryTheory Limits AlgebraicGeometry TopologicalSpace

universe u

/-- A category with zero morphisms together with a distinguished class of short exact sequences
`A ⟶ B ⟶ C` (recorded by the predicate `ses`), and a family of "diagonal" predicates `diag k`
on objects, indexed by a direction `k : ℕ`. For the exact category we start with (vector bundles
on a scheme) no object is diagonal; the binary complex construction `ExactData.binary` then
creates the diagonal predicates direction by direction. -/
structure ExactData where
  /-- The objects. -/
  Obj : Type (u + 1)
  [cat : Category.{u} Obj]
  [zero : HasZeroMorphisms Obj]
  /-- `ses f g` records that `A ⟶ B ⟶ C` is a distinguished short exact sequence. -/
  ses : ∀ {A B C : Obj}, (A ⟶ B) → (B ⟶ C) → Prop
  /-- `diag k T` records that `T` is diagonal in direction `k`. -/
  diag : ℕ → Obj → Prop

attribute [instance] ExactData.cat ExactData.zero

namespace ExactData

variable (D : ExactData.{u})

/-- A `ℤ`-graded object `X` with differential `d` (of degree `-1`) is *acyclic* if it is obtained
by splicing distinguished short exact sequences `Z i ⟶ X i ⟶ Z (i - 1)`, i.e. each differential
`d i : X i ⟶ X (i - 1)` factors as `X i ⟶ Z (i - 1) ⟶ X (i - 1)`. -/
def IsAcyclic (X : ℤ → D.Obj) (d : ∀ i, X i ⟶ X (i - 1)) : Prop :=
  ∃ (Z : ℤ → D.Obj) (ι : ∀ i, Z i ⟶ X i) (p : ∀ i, X i ⟶ Z (i - 1)),
    (∀ i, D.ses (ι i) (p i)) ∧ ∀ i, d i = p i ≫ ι (i - 1)

/-- A bounded acyclic binary complex in `D`: a bounded `ℤ`-graded object equipped with two
differentials (the "top" and the "bottom" differential), each of which makes it an acyclic
complex. -/
structure BinaryComplex where
  /-- The graded object. -/
  X : ℤ → D.Obj
  /-- The top differential. -/
  dTop : ∀ i, X i ⟶ X (i - 1)
  /-- The bottom differential. -/
  dBot : ∀ i, X i ⟶ X (i - 1)
  dTop_comp_dTop : ∀ i, (dTop i ≫ dTop (i - 1)) = 0
  dBot_comp_dBot : ∀ i, (dBot i ≫ dBot (i - 1)) = 0
  bounded : ∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ i, i < a ∨ b < i → IsZero (X i)
  isAcyclic_dTop : D.IsAcyclic X dTop
  isAcyclic_dBot : D.IsAcyclic X dBot

namespace BinaryComplex

variable {D}

/-- A morphism of binary complexes is a graded morphism commuting with both differentials. -/
@[ext]
structure Hom (T T' : D.BinaryComplex) where
  /-- The components of the morphism. -/
  f : ∀ i, T.X i ⟶ T'.X i
  comm_top : ∀ i, (T.dTop i ≫ f (i - 1)) = f i ≫ T'.dTop i
  comm_bot : ∀ i, (T.dBot i ≫ f (i - 1)) = f i ≫ T'.dBot i

instance : Category.{u} D.BinaryComplex where
  Hom := Hom
  id T := ⟨fun _ ↦ 𝟙 _, fun _ ↦ by simp, fun _ ↦ by simp⟩
  comp φ ψ := ⟨fun i ↦ φ.f i ≫ ψ.f i,
    fun i ↦ by rw [← Category.assoc, φ.comm_top, Category.assoc, ψ.comm_top, Category.assoc],
    fun i ↦ by rw [← Category.assoc, φ.comm_bot, Category.assoc, ψ.comm_bot, Category.assoc]⟩
  id_comp _ := Hom.ext (funext fun _ ↦ Category.id_comp _)
  comp_id _ := Hom.ext (funext fun _ ↦ Category.comp_id _)
  assoc _ _ _ := Hom.ext (funext fun _ ↦ Category.assoc _ _ _)

instance : HasZeroMorphisms D.BinaryComplex where
  zero _ _ := ⟨⟨fun _ ↦ 0, fun _ ↦ by simp, fun _ ↦ by simp⟩⟩
  comp_zero := by intros; exact Hom.ext (funext fun _ ↦ comp_zero)
  zero_comp := by intros; exact Hom.ext (funext fun _ ↦ zero_comp)

end BinaryComplex

/-- Grayson's binary complex construction `Bᑫ`: the objects are the bounded acyclic binary
complexes in `D`, a sequence of binary complexes is short exact if it is so in each degree, and
a binary complex is diagonal in direction `0` if its two differentials agree, and diagonal in
direction `k + 1` if all of its terms are diagonal in direction `k` in `D`. -/
def binary : ExactData.{u} where
  Obj := D.BinaryComplex
  ses φ ψ := ∀ i, D.ses (BinaryComplex.Hom.f φ i) (BinaryComplex.Hom.f ψ i)
  diag
    | 0, T => ∀ i, T.dTop i = T.dBot i
    | k + 1, T => ∀ i, D.diag k (T.X i)

/-- The subgroup of relations `[B] - [A] - [C]`, for every distinguished short exact sequence
`A ⟶ B ⟶ C`, defining `K₀`. -/
def K₀Relations : AddSubgroup (FreeAbelianGroup D.Obj) :=
  AddSubgroup.closure {x | ∃ (A B C : D.Obj) (f : A ⟶ B) (g : B ⟶ C), D.ses f g ∧
    x = FreeAbelianGroup.of B - FreeAbelianGroup.of A - FreeAbelianGroup.of C}

/-- The Grothendieck group `K₀ D`: the free abelian group on the objects of `D` modulo the
relations `[B] = [A] + [C]` for every distinguished short exact sequence `A ⟶ B ⟶ C`. -/
abbrev K₀ : Type (u + 1) := FreeAbelianGroup D.Obj ⧸ D.K₀Relations

/-- The class `[A]` of an object `A` in `K₀ D`. -/
def K₀.mk (A : D.Obj) : D.K₀ := QuotientAddGroup.mk (FreeAbelianGroup.of A)

/-- The `n`-fold iterate `(Bᑫ)ⁿ D` of the binary complex construction. Its objects are the
`n`-dimensional bounded acyclic binary multicomplexes in `D`. -/
def iterBinary : ℕ → ExactData.{u}
  | 0 => D
  | n + 1 => (iterBinary n).binary

/-- The subgroup of `K₀ ((Bᑫ)ⁿ D)` generated by the classes of the binary multicomplexes whose
top and bottom differentials agree in at least one direction. -/
def diagonalClasses (n : ℕ) : AddSubgroup (D.iterBinary n).K₀ :=
  AddSubgroup.closure {x | ∃ (T : (D.iterBinary n).Obj) (k : ℕ),
    (D.iterBinary n).diag k T ∧ x = K₀.mk _ T}

/-- Grayson's presentation of the `n`-th algebraic `K`-group of `D` [Gra2012, Corollary 7.4]:
the Grothendieck group of `n`-dimensional bounded acyclic binary multicomplexes in `D`, modulo
the classes of those that are diagonal in at least one direction. -/
abbrev K (n : ℕ) : Type (u + 1) := (D.iterBinary n).K₀ ⧸ D.diagonalClasses n

end ExactData

section Scheme

variable (X : Scheme.{u})

/-- The category of vector bundles on a scheme `X`, i.e. the full subcategory of `𝒪ₓ`-modules
that are locally free of finite rank. -/
abbrev VectorBundle : Type (u + 1) :=
  ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory (fun M : X.Modules ↦
    Nonempty (SheafOfModules.FiniteRankVectorBundleData (J := Opens.grothendieckTopology X) M))

/-- A sequence `A ⟶ B ⟶ C` of vector bundles on `X` is short exact if `0 ⟶ A ⟶ B ⟶ C ⟶ 0` is a
short exact sequence of `𝒪ₓ`-modules. -/
def VectorBundle.IsShortExact {A B C : VectorBundle X} (f : A ⟶ B) (g : B ⟶ C) : Prop :=
  ∃ w : (f.hom ≫ g.hom) = 0, (ShortComplex.mk f.hom g.hom w).ShortExact

/-- The exact category of vector bundles on a scheme `X`, with the short exact sequences of
`VectorBundle.IsShortExact`. No object is declared diagonal. -/
def vectorBundles : ExactData.{u} where
  Obj := VectorBundle X
  ses f g := VectorBundle.IsShortExact X f g
  diag _ _ := False

/-- The `n`-th algebraic `K`-group `K_n(X)` of a scheme `X`: the `K`-theory of the exact
category of vector bundles on `X`, in Grayson's presentation `ExactData.K`. -/
abbrev KGroup (n : ℕ) : Type (u + 1) := (vectorBundles X).K n

/-- In degree `0`, no relation is imposed beyond those of the Grothendieck group: `K₀(X)` is the
usual Grothendieck group of vector bundles on `X`. -/
@[category API, AMS 14 19]
theorem diagonalClasses_vectorBundles_zero : (vectorBundles X).diagonalClasses 0 = ⊥ := by
  rw [ExactData.diagonalClasses, AddSubgroup.closure_eq_bot_iff]
  rintro x ⟨T, k, hT, rfl⟩
  exact hT.elim

/-- `K₀(X)` in the sense of `KGroup` is the usual Grothendieck group of vector bundles on `X`. -/
@[category API, AMS 14 19]
theorem nonempty_kGroup_zero_addEquiv : Nonempty (KGroup X 0 ≃+ (vectorBundles X).K₀) :=
  ⟨(QuotientAddGroup.quotientAddEquivOfEq (diagonalClasses_vectorBundles_zero X)).trans
    QuotientAddGroup.quotientBot⟩

end Scheme

/-- A morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S` is projective if it factors as a closed immersion into some
projective space `ℙⁿ_S` followed by the projection to `S`. -/
def IsProjective {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (ι : X ⟶ ℙ(Fin n; S)), IsClosedImmersion ι ∧ (ι ≫ pullback.fst _ _) = f

/-- **Parshin's conjecture**: for any smooth projective variety $X$ over a finite field
$\mathbb{F}_q$, the higher algebraic $K$-groups of $X$ vanish up to torsion, i.e.
$K_i(X) \otimes \mathbb{Q} = 0$ for all $i > 0$; equivalently, each $K_i(X)$, $i > 0$, is a
torsion abelian group.

Here a variety over $\mathbb{F}_q$ is an integral scheme `X` with a morphism `f : X ⟶ Spec 𝔽_q`,
which is assumed to be smooth and projective. -/
@[category research open, AMS 14 19]
theorem parshins_conjecture (k : Type u) [Field k] [Finite k] (X : Scheme.{u})
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsIntegral X] [IsSmooth f] (hf : IsProjective f)
    (i : ℕ) (hi : 0 < i) :
    AddMonoid.IsTorsion (KGroup X i) := by
  sorry

end ParshinsConjecture
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot decomposition is correct: the statement is one universally quantified proposition (over finite fields, smooth projective varieties, and degrees i > 0); the dimension 0 and 1 cases in the article are known results, not separate conjectures.
modeling_decisions: Higher K-groups: Mathlib has no algebraic K-theory (no Q-construction, S-construction, or homotopy groups of nerves usable here). K_n(X) is defined via Grayson's presentation [Grayson, 'Algebraic K-theory via binary complexes', JAMS 25 (2012), Cor. 7.4]: K_n(N) ≅ K₀((B^q)^n N) / ⟨[T] : T diagonal in at least one direction⟩ for any exact category N. This is a theorem-backed equivalent description of Quillen's K_n, not the primary definition; a reviewer should check that they accept it as a faithful definition of 'the higher algebraic K-groups'. Grayson's ingredients are transcribed literally: bounded ℤ-graded complexes, acyclicity as splicing of admissible short exact sequences, degreewise short exact sequences in B^q, and the diagonal predicate tracked per direction (`ExactData.diag k`) so that 'diagonal in at least one direction' is `∃ k, diag k T` (not the weaker 'each slice diagonal in some direction').

K-theory of the scheme X is taken to be the K-theory of the exact category of vector bundles (locally free 𝒪_X-modules of finite rank, rank allowed to vary, via the repo's `SheafOfModules.FiniteRankVectorBundleData`), with a sequence A ⟶ B ⟶ C declared exact iff 0 → A → B → C → 0 is short exact in the abelian category `X.Modules` (Mathlib's `ShortComplex.ShortExact`). This is Quillen's K-theory of a scheme; it agrees with Thomason–Trobaugh K-theory for (quasi-)projective schemes.
'Vanish up to torsion' (K_i(X) ⊗ ℚ = 0) is formalized as `AddMonoid.IsTorsion (KGroup X i)`, i.e. every element has finite order; for abelian groups this is equivalent to K_i(X) ⊗_ℤ ℚ = 0.
'Higher' K-groups: degrees i with 0 < i (K_0 excluded), as in the article's displayed formula `K_i(X) ⊗ Q = 0, i > 0`.

'Smooth projective variety over a finite field': k is a `Field` with `Finite k`; X is a `Scheme` with a morphism f : X ⟶ Spec k that is `IsSmooth` (Mathlib) and projective; 'variety' is read as `IsIntegral X` (integral scheme; separatedness and finite type follow from projectivity). Since a smooth projective k-scheme is a finite disjoint union of such varieties and K-theory of a disjoint union is a product, dropping `IsIntegral` would give an equivalent statement.

Projectivity is not in Mathlib; `IsProjective f` is defined as: there exist n and a closed immersion ι : X ⟶ ℙ(Fin n; S) (the repo's `ProjectiveSpace`) with ι ≫ pullback.fst = f. Over a field this coincides with all standard notions of a projective morphism/variety.

Universe choice: `ExactData` fixes objects in `Type (u+1)` with hom-types in `Type u` so that the binary-complex construction can be iterated on the same type; this matches `X.Modules` for `X : Scheme.{u}`.
The repo's global asymptotic notation `≫` (in FormalConjecturesForMathlib) clashes with categorical composition, so compositions on the left of `=` are parenthesized; this is purely syntactic.

Two `@[category API]` sanity checks are included and proved: `diagonalClasses_vectorBundles_zero` (no diagonal relations in degree 0) and `nonempty_kGroup_zero_addEquiv` (K_0 in this presentation is the usual Grothendieck group of vector bundles).

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Parshin's conjecture

Parshin's conjecture (also called the Beilinson–Parshin conjecture) states that for any smooth
projective variety $X$ over a finite field, the higher algebraic K-groups vanish up to torsion:
$K_i(X) \otimes \mathbb{Q} = 0$ for all $i > 0$.

Mathlib has no definition of higher algebraic K-theory, so this file defines the K-groups of the
exact category of vector bundles on a scheme from scratch, using Waldhausen's $S_\bullet$
construction: $K_i(X) = \pi_{i+1}(|iS_\bullet \mathrm{Vect}(X)|)$, where $i$ denotes the
subcategory of isomorphisms. The geometric realisation of the bisimplicial set
$N_\bullet(iS_\bullet \mathrm{Vect}(X))$ is computed as the realisation of its diagonal.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parshin%27s_conjecture)
- [Ka05] B. Kahn, *Algebraic K-theory, algebraic cycles and arithmetic geometry*, Handbook of
  K-theory I, Springer (2005).
- [Wa85] F. Waldhausen, *Algebraic K-theory of spaces*, Lecture Notes in Math. 1126 (1985),
  §1.3–1.4 (the $S_\bullet$ construction).
- [We13] C. Weibel, *The K-book: An Introduction to Algebraic K-theory*, GSM 145, AMS (2013),
  Chapter IV, §6 (K-theory of exact categories and schemes) and §8 (Waldhausen K-theory).
-/

open CategoryTheory Limits AlgebraicGeometry Simplicial ZeroObject

namespace ParshinsConjecture

universe u v

noncomputable section

/- ## Waldhausen's `S_•` construction for a fully exact subcategory of an abelian category -/

namespace KTheory

/-- The poset $[n] \times \mathrm{Ar}[n]$ indexing the $n$-simplices of the diagonal of the
bisimplicial set $N_\bullet(iS_\bullet)$: triples $(p, i, j)$ with $0 \le i \le j \le n$, where
$p$ is the nerve direction and $(i, j)$ is an object of the arrow category $\mathrm{Ar}[n]$ of the
poset $[n]$. -/
abbrev SIndex (n : ℕ) : Type :=
  {t : Fin (n + 1) × Fin (n + 1) × Fin (n + 1) // t.2.1 ≤ t.2.2}

namespace SIndex

variable {a b : SimplexCategory}

/-- The map $[m] \times \mathrm{Ar}[m] \to [n] \times \mathrm{Ar}[n]$ induced by a morphism
$[m] \to [n]$ of the simplex category. -/
def map (θ : a ⟶ b) (t : SIndex a.len) : SIndex b.len :=
  ⟨(θ.toOrderHom t.1.1, θ.toOrderHom t.1.2.1, θ.toOrderHom t.1.2.2), θ.toOrderHom.monotone t.2⟩

@[category API, AMS 18]
lemma monotone_map (θ : a ⟶ b) : Monotone (map θ) := fun _ _ h =>
  ⟨θ.toOrderHom.monotone h.1, θ.toOrderHom.monotone h.2.1, θ.toOrderHom.monotone h.2.2⟩

end SIndex

variable {A : Type u} [Category.{v} A]

/-- In a functor out of a preorder, the image of a morphism $x \to y$ factors through any
intermediate element $x \le z \le y$. -/
@[category API, AMS 18]
lemma map_eq_map_comp_map {C : Type*} [Preorder C] (F : C ⥤ A) {x y z : C} (f : x ⟶ y)
    (h₁ : x ≤ z) (h₂ : z ≤ y) :
    F.map f = CategoryStruct.comp (F.map (homOfLE h₁)) (F.map (homOfLE h₂)) := by
  rw [← F.map_comp]
  exact congrArg F.map (Subsingleton.elim _ _)

variable [Abelian A]

/-- If a functor $F$ on $[n] \times \mathrm{Ar}[n]$ sends every $(p, j, j)$ to a zero object, then
the composite $F(p, i, j) \to F(p, i, k) \to F(p, j, k)$ is zero for $i \le j \le k$. -/
@[category API, AMS 18]
lemma map_comp_eq_zero {n : ℕ} (F : SIndex n ⥤ A)
    (hF : ∀ (p i : Fin (n + 1)), IsZero (F.obj ⟨(p, i, i), le_rfl⟩))
    (p : Fin (n + 1)) {i j k : Fin (n + 1)} (hij : i ≤ j) (hjk : j ≤ k) :
    CategoryStruct.comp
      (F.map (homOfLE ⟨le_rfl, le_rfl, hjk⟩ :
        (⟨(p, i, j), hij⟩ : SIndex n) ⟶ ⟨(p, i, k), hij.trans hjk⟩))
      (F.map (homOfLE ⟨le_rfl, hij, le_rfl⟩ :
        (⟨(p, i, k), hij.trans hjk⟩ : SIndex n) ⟶ ⟨(p, j, k), hjk⟩)) = 0 := by
  rw [← F.map_comp, map_eq_map_comp_map F _
    (⟨le_rfl, hij, le_rfl⟩ : (⟨(p, i, j), hij⟩ : SIndex n) ≤ ⟨(p, j, j), le_rfl⟩)
    (⟨le_rfl, le_rfl, hjk⟩ : (⟨(p, j, j), le_rfl⟩ : SIndex n) ≤ ⟨(p, j, k), hjk⟩),
    (hF p j).eq_of_tgt (F.map _) 0, zero_comp]

/-- Let `P` be a property of objects of an abelian category `A`, thought of as the fully exact
subcategory of `A` consisting of the objects satisfying `P` (with the short exact sequences of `A`
as admissible exact sequences). A functor $F \colon [n] \times \mathrm{Ar}[n] \to A$ is an
$n$-simplex of the diagonal of the bisimplicial set $N_\bullet(iS_\bullet P)$ if:
* every $F(p, i, j)$ satisfies `P`;
* every $F(p, j, j)$ is a zero object;
* for every $p$ and $i \le j \le k$, the sequence $F(p, i, j) \to F(p, i, k) \to F(p, j, k)$ is a
  short exact sequence in `A` (so that each $F(p, -, -)$ is an object of Waldhausen's $S_n P$);
* for every $p \le q$ and $i \le j$, the morphism $F(p, i, j) \to F(q, i, j)$ is an isomorphism
  (so that the morphisms $F(p, -, -) \to F(q, -, -)$ in $S_n P$ are isomorphisms). -/
structure IsSimplex (P : ObjectProperty A) {n : ℕ} (F : SIndex n ⥤ A) : Prop where
  prop : ∀ t, P (F.obj t)
  isZero : ∀ (p i : Fin (n + 1)), IsZero (F.obj ⟨(p, i, i), le_rfl⟩)
  shortExact : ∀ (p : Fin (n + 1)) {i j k : Fin (n + 1)} (hij : i ≤ j) (hjk : j ≤ k),
    (ShortComplex.mk _ _ (map_comp_eq_zero F isZero p hij hjk)).ShortExact
  isIso : ∀ {p q : Fin (n + 1)} (hpq : p ≤ q) {i j : Fin (n + 1)} (hij : i ≤ j),
    IsIso (F.map (homOfLE ⟨hpq, le_rfl, le_rfl⟩ :
      (⟨(p, i, j), hij⟩ : SIndex n) ⟶ ⟨(q, i, j), hij⟩))

variable (P : ObjectProperty A)

/-- Simplices are stable under restriction along maps of the simplex category. -/
@[category API, AMS 18 19]
lemma IsSimplex.map {a b : SimplexCategory} (θ : a ⟶ b) {F : SIndex b.len ⥤ A}
    (hF : IsSimplex P F) : IsSimplex P ((SIndex.monotone_map θ).functor ⋙ F) where
  prop _ := hF.prop _
  isZero p i := hF.isZero (θ.toOrderHom p) (θ.toOrderHom i)
  shortExact p _ _ _ hij hjk :=
    hF.shortExact (θ.toOrderHom p) (θ.toOrderHom.monotone hij) (θ.toOrderHom.monotone hjk)
  isIso hpq _ _ hij := hF.isIso (θ.toOrderHom.monotone hpq) (θ.toOrderHom.monotone hij)

/-- The diagonal of the bisimplicial set $N_\bullet(iS_\bullet P)$, where $S_\bullet P$ is
Waldhausen's $S_\bullet$ construction applied to the fully exact subcategory of `A` of objects
satisfying `P`, and $iS_n P$ is its subcategory of isomorphisms. Its geometric realisation is
(homeomorphic to) the realisation of the bisimplicial set, so its loop space is the K-theory space
of the exact category. -/
def sSet : SSet.{max u v} where
  obj Δ := {F : SIndex Δ.unop.len ⥤ A // IsSimplex P F}
  map θ F := ⟨(SIndex.monotone_map θ.unop).functor ⋙ F.1, F.2.map P θ.unop⟩
  map_id _ := rfl
  map_comp _ _ := rfl

/-- The vertex of `KTheory.sSet P` given by a zero object `Z` satisfying `P`. -/
def vertex (Z : A) (hZ : IsZero Z) (hP : P Z) : (sSet P).obj (Opposite.op ⦋0⦌) :=
  ⟨(Functor.const _).obj Z,
    { prop := fun _ => hP
      isZero := fun _ _ => hZ
      shortExact := by
        intros
        exact ShortComplex.ShortExact.mk' (ShortComplex.exact_of_isZero_X₂ _ hZ)
          ⟨fun g h _ => hZ.eq_of_tgt g h⟩ ⟨fun g h _ => hZ.eq_of_src g h⟩
      isIso := by
        intros
        exact (inferInstance : IsIso (𝟙 Z)) }⟩

/-- The base point of the geometric realisation $|iS_\bullet P|$ corresponding to the vertex
`KTheory.vertex P Z hZ hP`. -/
def basePoint (Z : A) (hZ : IsZero Z) (hP : P Z) : SSet.toTop.obj (sSet P) :=
  SSet.toTop.map (SSet.yonedaEquiv.symm (vertex P Z hZ hP))
    ((SSet.toTopSimplex.inv.app ⦋0⦌) default)

/-- The $i$-th algebraic K-group of the fully exact subcategory of `A` of objects satisfying `P`:
$K_i = \pi_i(\Omega |iS_\bullet P|) = \pi_{i+1}(|iS_\bullet P|)$, based at the vertex given by
the zero object `Z`. -/
abbrev KGroup (Z : A) (hZ : IsZero Z) (hP : P Z) (i : ℕ) : Type (max u v) :=
  HomotopyGroup.Pi (i + 1) (SSet.toTop.obj (sSet P)) (basePoint P Z hZ hP)

end KTheory

/- ## The algebraic K-theory of a scheme -/

variable {X : Scheme.{u}}

/-- An $\mathcal{O}_X$-module `M` on a scheme `X` is a vector bundle if it is locally free of
finite rank: every point has an open neighbourhood `U` such that the restriction of `M` to `U` is
isomorphic to a free $\mathcal{O}_U$-module on a finite index type. -/
def IsVectorBundle (M : X.Modules) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : X, ∃ (U : X.Opens), x ∈ U ∧ ∃ (ι : Type u), Finite ι ∧
    Nonempty (M.restrict U.ι ≅ SheafOfModules.free (R := U.toScheme.ringCatSheaf) ι)

variable (X) in
/-- The zero module is a vector bundle (of rank zero). -/
@[category API, AMS 14]
lemma isVectorBundle_zero : IsVectorBundle (0 : X.Modules) := by
  intro x
  refine ⟨⊤, trivial, PEmpty, inferInstance, ⟨IsZero.iso ?_ ?_⟩⟩
  · exact IsZero.of_iso ((Scheme.Modules.pullback _).map_isZero (isZero_zero _))
      ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctorIsoPullback _).app 0)
  · exact (isColimitEquivIsInitialOfIsEmpty _ _
      (SheafOfModules.isColimitFreeCofan (R := (⊤ : X.Opens).toScheme.ringCatSheaf)
        PEmpty)).isZero

variable (X) in
/-- The $i$-th algebraic K-group $K_i(X)$ of a scheme `X`: the $i$-th K-group of the exact
category of vector bundles on `X` (locally free $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules of finite rank, with the
short exact sequences of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules as admissible exact sequences), defined via
Waldhausen's $S_\bullet$ construction and based at the zero module. -/
abbrev KGroup (i : ℕ) : Type (u + 1) :=
  KTheory.KGroup (IsVectorBundle (X := X)) 0 (isZero_zero _) (isVectorBundle_zero X) i

@[category test, AMS 19]
example (i : ℕ) : Group (KGroup X i) := inferInstance

/-- A morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ Y` is projective if it factors as a closed immersion
$X \to \mathbb{P}^n_Y$ followed by the projection $\mathbb{P}^n_Y \to Y$, for some $n$. -/
def IsProjective {Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (g : X ⟶ ℙ(Fin (n + 1); Y)), IsClosedImmersion g ∧ (g ≫ pullback.fst _ _) = f

/-- Projective space $\mathbb{P}^n_Y$ is projective over $Y$. -/
@[category test, AMS 14]
lemma isProjective_projectiveSpace {Y : Scheme.{u}} (n : ℕ) :
    IsProjective (pullback.fst _ _ : ℙ(Fin (n + 1); Y) ⟶ Y) :=
  ⟨n, 𝟙 _, inferInstance, Category.id_comp _⟩

/-- **Parshin's conjecture.** Let $X$ be a smooth projective variety defined over a finite field
$k$. Then the higher algebraic K-groups of $X$ vanish up to torsion: $K_i(X) \otimes \mathbb{Q} = 0$
for all $i > 0$, i.e. every element of $K_i(X)$ has finite order.

Here `X` is a variety over `k` through the structure morphism `f : X ⟶ Spec k`, which is required
to be smooth and projective, and `X` is required to be integral. -/
@[category research open, AMS 14 19]
theorem parshins_conjecture (k : Type u) [Field k] [Finite k] (X : Scheme.{u})
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsSmooth f] (hf : IsProjective f) [IsIntegral X] (i : ℕ)
    (hi : 0 < i) : Monoid.IsTorsion (KGroup X i) := by
  sorry

end

end ParshinsConjecture

modeling_decisions: Higher K-groups: Mathlib has no algebraic K-theory. The file defines K_i(X) := π_{i+1}(|iS_• Vect(X)|, 0) using Waldhausen's S_• construction (Waldhausen 1985 §1.3; Weibel K-book IV.8) applied to the exact category of vector bundles on X, with the standard identification K_i = π_i(Ω|iS_•|) = π_{i+1}(|iS_•|). This is one of the standard equivalent definitions of the K-theory of an exact category (agrees with Quillen's Q-construction by Waldhausen's/Weibel's comparison theorem), and Quillen's K(X) := K(Vect(X)) is the standard K-theory of a scheme (agrees with Thomason–Trobaugh for quasi-projective X).

The bisimplicial set N_•(iS_•) is encoded by its diagonal: an n-simplex is a functor F from the poset [n] × Ar[n] (triples (p,i,j), i ≤ j; `KTheory.SIndex n`) to the abelian category such that all values are vector bundles, F(p,j,j) is a zero object, F(p,i,j) → F(p,i,k) → F(p,j,k) is a short exact sequence in X.Modules for all i ≤ j ≤ k, and F(p,i,j) → F(q,i,j) is an iso for p ≤ q. Realisation of the diagonal is homeomorphic to realisation of the bisimplicial set. Zero objects are required only up to isomorphism (IsZero) rather than being a fixed chosen zero object; this gives a levelwise equivalent simplicial category, hence the same homotopy type. Degenerate cases i = j or j = k in the exactness condition are automatically satisfied and impose no extra restriction.

Exact structure: the admissible short exact sequences of Vect(X) are the sequences that are short exact in the abelian category `X.Modules` of all O_X-modules (the standard exact structure on vector bundles).

Vector bundle (`IsVectorBundle`): an O_X-module M such that every point has an open neighbourhood U with `M.restrict U.ι ≅ SheafOfModules.free ι` for some finite type ι (locally free of finite rank). Rank is allowed to vary between components.

'Vanish up to torsion' (K_i(X) ⊗ ℚ = 0) is formalised as `Monoid.IsTorsion (KGroup X i)` (every element has finite order); K_i(X) carries the group structure `HomotopyGroup.group`. 'Higher' is `0 < i`, so K_0 is excluded.

Base point: the vertex given by the constant functor at the zero module `0 : X.Modules` (proved to be a vector bundle in `isVectorBundle_zero`). The realisation is path-connected so the choice does not affect the homotopy groups.

'Smooth projective variety over a finite field k': `[Field k] [Finite k]`, `f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)` with Mathlib's `[IsSmooth f]`, `IsProjective f` (bespoke: f factors as a closed immersion into ℙ^n_k = `ℙ(Fin (n+1); Spec k)` from FormalConjecturesForMathlib followed by `pullback.fst`, Hartshorne's definition), and `[IsIntegral X]` for 'variety'. Including integrality follows the usual meaning of 'variety'; the conjecture for all smooth projective k-schemes is equivalent since such a scheme is a finite disjoint union of smooth projective integral varieties and K-theory of a disjoint union is the product.
Separatedness and finite type are not stated separately since they follow from projectivity.

Because the repository defines a global `≫` notation for big-O (FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Analysis/Asymptotics/Basic.lean), categorical composition is written as `(g ≫ pullback.fst _ _)` with parentheses or `CategoryStruct.comp`.

/-!
# Parshin's conjecture

Parshin's conjecture (also called the Beilinson–Parshin conjecture) states that for every
smooth projective variety $X$ over a finite field, the higher algebraic K-groups of $X$
vanish up to torsion: $K_i(X) \otimes \mathbb{Q} = 0$ for all $i > 0$.

Mathlib has no definition of higher algebraic K-theory, so this file constructs the
algebraic K-groups of a scheme from scratch, following Waldhausen:

* `IsVectorBundle X M` says that the sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules `M` is locally free of
  finite rank. The full subcategory of `X.Modules` on these objects, together with the short
  exact sequences of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules, is the exact category of vector bundles on $X$.
* For an abelian category `A` and a property `P` of objects of `A` (thought of as an exact
  subcategory of `A`), `sConstruction P : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ ⥤ Cat` is Waldhausen's
  $S_\bullet$-construction: `S_n P` is the category of functors `Ar[n] ⥤ A` sending
  `(i, j)` to an object `F(i, j)` satisfying `P`, with `F(i, i)` zero and with
  `F(i, j) → F(i, k) → F(j, k)` short exact for all `i ≤ j ≤ k`.
* `kSpace P` is the geometric realization $|iS_\bullet P|$ of the bisimplicial set
  $N_\bullet iS_\bullet P$ whose $(n, k)$-simplices are strings of $k$ composable
  isomorphisms in $S_n P$. Waldhausen's K-theory space is the loop space
  $\Omega |iS_\bullet P|$, so that `KGroup P _ i` is $K_i(P) = \pi_{i+1}(|iS_\bullet P|, ∗)$
  with base point the zero object. For an exact category this agrees with Quillen's
  K-theory by Waldhausen's comparison theorem [Wa85, §1.9].
* `algebraicKGroup X i` is the `i`-th algebraic K-group $K_i(X)$ of the scheme `X`, namely
  the `i`-th K-group of the exact category of vector bundles on `X`.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia, Parshin's conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parshin%27s_conjecture)
* [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
* [Wa85] F. Waldhausen, *Algebraic K-theory of spaces*, Lecture Notes in Math. 1126 (1985),
  318–419.
* [Ka05] B. Kahn, *Algebraic K-theory, algebraic cycles and arithmetic geometry*,
  Handbook of K-theory I, Springer (2005).
-/

/- ### Waldhausen's `S_•`-construction -/

section SConstruction

variable {A : Type u} [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A]

/-- The object `(i, j)` of the arrow category `Ar[n]` of the poset `[n] = {0 < 1 < ⋯ < n}`,
for `i ≤ j`. -/
abbrev arrowOfLE {n : ℕ} {i j : Fin (n + 1)} (h : i ≤ j) : Arrow (Fin (n + 1)) :=
  Arrow.mk (homOfLE h)

/-- A functor `F : Ar[n] ⥤ A` is an object of Waldhausen's `S_n P` if all its values `F(i, j)`
satisfy `P`, its values `F(i, i)` on the diagonal are zero objects, and for all `i ≤ j ≤ k` the
sequence `F(i, j) → F(i, k) → F(j, k)` is a short exact sequence in `A`. -/
structure IsSObj (P : ObjectProperty A) {n : ℕ} (F : Arrow (Fin (n + 1)) ⥤ A) : Prop where
  /-- Every value `F(i, j)` satisfies `P`. -/
  prop : ∀ a, P (F.obj a)
  /-- The values `F(i, i)` on the diagonal are zero objects. -/
  isZero : ∀ i : Fin (n + 1), IsZero (F.obj (arrowOfLE (le_refl i)))
  /-- For `i ≤ j ≤ k`, the sequence `F(i, j) → F(i, k) → F(j, k)` is short exact. -/
  shortExact : ∀ (i j k : Fin (n + 1)) (hij : i ≤ j) (hjk : j ≤ k),
    ∃ w, (ShortComplex.mk
      (F.map (Arrow.homMk (f := arrowOfLE hij) (g := arrowOfLE (hij.trans hjk))
        (𝟙 i) (homOfLE hjk) (Subsingleton.elim _ _)))
      (F.map (Arrow.homMk (f := arrowOfLE (hij.trans hjk)) (g := arrowOfLE hjk)
        (homOfLE hij) (𝟙 k) (Subsingleton.elim _ _))) w).ShortExact

variable (P : ObjectProperty A)

/-- The objects of `S_n P`, as a property of functors `Ar[n] ⥤ A`. -/
def sProp (n : SimplexCategory) : ObjectProperty (Arrow (Fin (n.len + 1)) ⥤ A) :=
  fun F => IsSObj P F

/-- The property `IsSObj P` is stable under precomposition with the functor `Ar[m] ⥤ Ar[n]`
induced by a monotone map `θ : [m] → [n]`; this gives the simplicial structure of `S_• P`. -/
@[category API, AMS 18 19]
lemma IsSObj.comp {m n : SimplexCategory} (θ : m ⟶ n) {F : Arrow (Fin (n.len + 1)) ⥤ A}
    (hF : IsSObj P F) : IsSObj P (θ.toOrderHom.monotone.functor.mapArrow ⋙ F) where
  prop _ := hF.prop _
  isZero i := hF.isZero (θ.toOrderHom i)
  shortExact _ _ _ hij hjk :=
    hF.shortExact _ _ _ (θ.toOrderHom.monotone hij) (θ.toOrderHom.monotone hjk)

/-- Waldhausen's `S_•`-construction of `P`, as a simplicial category: `S_n P` is the full
subcategory of `Ar[n] ⥤ A` on the objects satisfying `IsSObj P`, and a monotone map
`θ : [m] → [n]` acts by precomposition with the induced functor `Ar[m] ⥤ Ar[n]`. -/
def sConstruction : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ ⥤ Cat where
  obj n := Cat.of (sProp P n.unop).FullSubcategory
  map θ := Functor.toCatHom <| (sProp P _).lift ((sProp P _).ι ⋙
    (Functor.whiskeringLeft _ _ A).obj θ.unop.toOrderHom.monotone.functor.mapArrow)
    (fun F => F.2.comp P θ.unop)
  map_id _ := rfl
  map_comp _ _ := rfl

end SConstruction

/- ### The K-theory space and the K-groups -/

/-- The core (the groupoid of isomorphisms) of a category, as a functor `Cat ⥤ Cat`. -/
def coreFunctor : Cat.{v, u} ⥤ Cat.{v, u} where
  obj C := Cat.of (Core C)
  map F := F.toFunctor.core.toCatHom
  map_id _ := rfl
  map_comp _ _ := rfl

/-- The diagonal simplicial set of a bisimplicial set. -/
def diagonal (B : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ ⥤ SSet.{u}) : SSet.{u} :=
  Functor.diag _ ⋙ Functor.uncurry.obj B

section KTheory

variable {A : Type u} [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A] (P : ObjectProperty A)

/-- The diagonal of the bisimplicial set `N_• iS_• P`, whose `(n, k)`-simplices are strings of
`k` composable isomorphisms in `S_n P`. -/
def kSimplicialSet : SSet := diagonal (sConstruction P ⋙ coreFunctor ⋙ nerveFunctor)

/-- The geometric realization `|iS_• P|`. Waldhausen's K-theory space of `P` is the loop space
of this space. -/
noncomputable def kSpace : TopCat := SSet.toTop.obj (kSimplicialSet P)

/-- The object of `S_0 P` given by the constant functor at the zero object. -/
noncomputable def zeroSObj (hP : P 0) : (sProp P ⦋0⦌).FullSubcategory where
  obj := (Functor.const _).obj 0
  property :=
    { prop := fun _ => hP
      isZero := fun _ => isZero_zero A
      shortExact := fun _ _ _ _ _ => ⟨(isZero_zero A).eq_of_src _ _,
        { exact := ShortComplex.exact_of_isZero_X₂ _ (isZero_zero A)
          mono_f := by dsimp; infer_instance
          epi_g := by dsimp; infer_instance }⟩ }

/-- The base point of `kSpace P`: the vertex given by the zero object. -/
noncomputable def kBasepoint (hP : P 0) : kSpace P :=
  TopCat.toSSetObjEquiv _ _
    ((sSetTopAdj.unit.app (kSimplicialSet P)).app (Opposite.op ⦋0⦌)
      (ComposableArrows.mk₀ (Core.mk (zeroSObj P hP))))
    ⟨_, ite_eq_mem_stdSimplex ℝ (0 : Fin 1)⟩

/-- The `i`-th K-group `K_i P = π_{i+1}(|iS_• P|, ∗)` of `P`, where `∗` is the vertex given by
the zero object. -/
noncomputable abbrev KGroup (hP : P 0) (i : ℕ) : Type _ :=
  π_ (i + 1) (kSpace P) (kBasepoint P hP)

end KTheory

/- ### Vector bundles and the algebraic K-theory of a scheme -/

section VectorBundles

variable (X : Scheme.{u})

/-- A sheaf of `𝒪_X`-modules `M` is a vector bundle (i.e. locally free of finite rank) if
every point has an open neighbourhood `U` such that the restriction of `M` to `U` is
isomorphic to a free `𝒪_U`-module of some finite rank `n`. -/
def IsVectorBundle (M : X.Modules) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : X, ∃ (U : X.Opens) (n : ℕ), x ∈ U ∧
    Nonempty (M.restrict U.ι ≅
      SheafOfModules.free (R := (U : Scheme.{u}).ringCatSheaf) (ULift.{u} (Fin n)))

/-- The zero sheaf is a vector bundle (of rank `0`). -/
@[category API, AMS 14]
theorem isVectorBundle_zero : IsVectorBundle X 0 :=
  fun _ => ⟨⊤, 0, trivial, ⟨IsZero.iso
    ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor _).map_isZero (isZero_zero _))
    ((isColimitEquivIsInitialOfIsEmpty _ (colimit.cocone _) (colimit.isColimit _)).isZero)⟩⟩

/-- The `i`-th algebraic K-group `K_i(X)` of a scheme `X`, defined as the `i`-th K-group of the
exact category of vector bundles on `X` (with base point the zero vector bundle). -/
noncomputable abbrev algebraicKGroup (i : ℕ) : Type _ :=
  KGroup (IsVectorBundle X) (isVectorBundle_zero X) i

end VectorBundles

/-- A morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S` is projective if it factors as a closed immersion
`X ⟶ ℙ^n_S` followed by the projection `ℙ^n_S ⟶ S`, for some `n`. -/
def IsProjective {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (g : X ⟶ ℙ(Fin (n + 1); S)),
    IsClosedImmersion g ∧ CategoryStruct.comp g (pullback.fst _ _) = f

/--
**Parshin's conjecture.** Let $X$ be a smooth projective variety over a finite field $k$.
Then the higher algebraic K-groups of $X$ vanish up to torsion: for every $i > 0$,
$K_i(X) \otimes \mathbb{Q} = 0$, i.e. every element of $K_i(X)$ has finite order.

Here a variety over $k$ is an integral scheme `X` with a morphism `f : X ⟶ Spec k`; it is
smooth (resp. projective) if `f` is.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 14 19]
theorem parshins_conjecture {k : Type u} [Field k] [Finite k] (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X]
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsSmooth f] (hf : IsProjective f) (i : ℕ) (hi : 0 < i) :
    Monoid.IsTorsion (algebraicKGroup X i) := by
  sorry

end ParshinsConjecture

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Parshin's conjecture

Parshin's conjecture (also called the Beilinson–Parshin conjecture) states that for any smooth
projective variety $X$ over a finite field, the higher algebraic K-groups of $X$ vanish up to
torsion: $K_i(X) \otimes \mathbb{Q} = 0$ for all $i > 0$.

Mathlib has no definition of higher algebraic K-theory, so this file builds one. Following
Quillen, the K-theory of a scheme $X$ is the K-theory of the exact category $\mathcal{P}(X)$ of
vector bundles (locally free $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules of finite rank) on $X$, with the exact
sequences being those that are exact in the abelian category of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules. The
K-theory space of an exact category is defined here by Waldhausen's $S_\bullet$-construction,
which is naturally homotopy equivalent to Quillen's $Q$-construction ([Wa85], §1.9):
$K(\mathcal{P}) = \Omega |iS_\bullet \mathcal{P}|$ and $K_i(\mathcal{P}) = \pi_{i+1}
|iS_\bullet \mathcal{P}|$. Here $S_n \mathcal{P}$ is the category of functors
$\mathrm{Ar}[n] \to \mathcal{P}$, $(i \le j) \mapsto A_{ij}$, with $A_{ii} = 0$ and with
$A_{ij} \to A_{ik} \to A_{jk}$ short exact for all $i \le j \le k$; $iS_n \mathcal{P}$ is its
subcategory of isomorphisms; and $|iS_\bullet \mathcal{P}|$ is the geometric realization of
the diagonal of the bisimplicial set $([m], [n]) \mapsto N_m(iS_n \mathcal{P})$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Parshin's conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parshin%27s_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wa85] F. Waldhausen, *Algebraic K-theory of spaces*, Lecture Notes in Math. 1126 (1985),
  318–419.
- [Qu73] D. Quillen, *Higher algebraic K-theory: I*, Lecture Notes in Math. 341 (1973), 85–147.
- [Ka05] B. Kahn, *Algebraic K-theory, algebraic cycles and arithmetic geometry*, in Handbook of
  K-theory I, Springer (2005).
-/

open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite Simplicial Topology AlgebraicGeometry

namespace ParshinsConjecture

universe v u

section WaldhausenSConstruction

variable {A : Type u} [Category.{v} A] [HasZeroMorphisms A] (P : ObjectProperty A)

variable {n : ℕ}

/-- For `i ≤ j ≤ k` in `Fin (n + 1)`, the morphism `(i ≤ j) ⟶ (i ≤ k)` in the arrow category
`Arrow (Fin (n + 1))` given by `𝟙 i` on the left and `j ≤ k` on the right. -/
def arrowHomLeft {i j k : Fin (n + 1)} (hij : i ≤ j) (hjk : j ≤ k) :
    Arrow.mk (homOfLE hij) ⟶ Arrow.mk (homOfLE (hij.trans hjk)) :=
  Arrow.homMk (𝟙 i) (homOfLE hjk)

/-- For `i ≤ j ≤ k` in `Fin (n + 1)`, the morphism `(i ≤ k) ⟶ (j ≤ k)` in the arrow category
`Arrow (Fin (n + 1))` given by `i ≤ j` on the left and `𝟙 k` on the right. -/
def arrowHomRight {i j k : Fin (n + 1)} (hij : i ≤ j) (hjk : j ≤ k) :
    Arrow.mk (homOfLE (hij.trans hjk)) ⟶ Arrow.mk (homOfLE hjk) :=
  Arrow.homMk (homOfLE hij) (𝟙 k)

/-- Let `P` be a class of objects of a category `A` with zero morphisms; think of `P` as a full
subcategory of an abelian category `A`, made into an exact category by declaring a sequence exact
if it is exact in `A`. A functor `F : Arrow (Fin (Δ.len + 1)) ⥤ A`, `(i ≤ j) ↦ F(i, j)`, is an
object of the `Δ.len`-th stage `S_Δ P` of Waldhausen's `S`-construction of `P` if
* `F(i, i)` is a zero object for every `i`,
* every `F(i, j)` lies in `P`, and
* for all `i ≤ j ≤ k`, the sequence `F(i, j) ⟶ F(i, k) ⟶ F(j, k)` is short exact in `A`.

This is Waldhausen's definition ([Wa85], §1.3): a sequence of cofibrations (admissible
monomorphisms) `0 = F(0, 0) ↪ F(0, 1) ↪ ⋯ ↪ F(0, n)` together with compatible choices of
quotients `F(j, k) = F(0, k) / F(0, j)`. -/
def IsWaldhausenSimplex (Δ : SimplexCategory) :
    ObjectProperty (Arrow (Fin (Δ.len + 1)) ⥤ A) := fun F =>
  (∀ f : Arrow (Fin (Δ.len + 1)), f.left = f.right → IsZero (F.obj f)) ∧
  (∀ f : Arrow (Fin (Δ.len + 1)), P (F.obj f)) ∧
  (∀ (i j k : Fin (Δ.len + 1)) (hij : i ≤ j) (hjk : j ≤ k),
    ∃ (w : (F.map (arrowHomLeft hij hjk) ≫ F.map (arrowHomRight hij hjk)) = 0),
      (ShortComplex.mk _ _ w).ShortExact)

/-- Restricting a Waldhausen simplex along a monotone map `θ : Δ ⟶ Δ'` of simplices gives a
Waldhausen simplex. -/
@[category API, AMS 18 19]
lemma isWaldhausenSimplex_comp {Δ Δ' : SimplexCategory} (θ : Δ ⟶ Δ')
    (F : Arrow (Fin (Δ'.len + 1)) ⥤ A) (hF : IsWaldhausenSimplex P Δ' F) :
    IsWaldhausenSimplex P Δ ((SimplexCategory.toCat.map θ).toFunctor.mapArrow ⋙ F) := by
  obtain ⟨h0, hP, hex⟩ := hF
  refine ⟨fun f hf => h0 _ ?_, fun f => hP _, fun i j k hij hjk => ?_⟩
  · simp [hf]
  · exact hex _ _ _ (θ.toOrderHom.monotone hij) (θ.toOrderHom.monotone hjk)

/-- The simplicial structure maps of Waldhausen's `S`-construction: a monotone map `θ : Δ ⟶ Δ'`
induces the functor `S_Δ' P ⥤ S_Δ P` given by precomposition with `Arrow (θ)`. -/
def sConstructionMap {Δ Δ' : SimplexCategory} (θ : Δ ⟶ Δ') :
    (IsWaldhausenSimplex P Δ').FullSubcategory ⥤ (IsWaldhausenSimplex P Δ).FullSubcategory :=
  ObjectProperty.lift _ ((IsWaldhausenSimplex P Δ').ι ⋙
    (Functor.whiskeringLeft _ _ A).obj (SimplexCategory.toCat.map θ).toFunctor.mapArrow)
    (fun F => isWaldhausenSimplex_comp P θ F.obj F.property)

/-- Waldhausen's `S`-construction `iS_• P` of `P` (with isomorphisms as weak equivalences), as a
simplicial object in `Cat`: `⦋n⦌` is sent to the groupoid `iS_n P` of Waldhausen simplices in
`S_n P` and their isomorphisms, i.e. to the core of the full subcategory `S_n P` of
`Arrow (Fin (n + 1)) ⥤ A`. -/
def sConstruction : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ ⥤ Cat.{v, max u v} where
  obj Δ := Cat.of (Core (IsWaldhausenSimplex P Δ.unop).FullSubcategory)
  map θ := ((sConstructionMap P θ.unop).core).toCatHom
  map_id _ := rfl
  map_comp _ _ := rfl

/-- The simplicial set underlying `|iS_• P|`: the diagonal of the bisimplicial set
`(⦋m⦌, ⦋n⦌) ↦ N_m (iS_n P)` obtained by taking nerves levelwise in `sConstruction P`. -/
def kTheorySSet : SSet.{max u v} :=
  Functor.diag _ ⋙ Functor.uncurry.obj (sConstruction P ⋙ nerveFunctor)

/-- The space `|iS_• P|`, whose loop space is the K-theory space `K(P)` of the exact category
`P`: `K_i(P) = π_{i+1} |iS_• P|` for all `i ≥ 0`. It is path-connected (all vertices are the
zero functors, which are all isomorphic), so its homotopy groups do not depend on the choice of
basepoint. -/
noncomputable def kTheorySpace : TopCat.{max u v} := SSet.toTop.obj (kTheorySSet P)

end WaldhausenSConstruction

section Scheme

variable (X : Scheme.{u})

/-- An `𝒪ₓ`-module `M` on a scheme `X` is a vector bundle if it is locally free of finite rank:
there is an open cover of `X` on each member `U` of which `M` restricts to a free `𝒪_U`-module
on finitely many generators. -/
def IsVectorBundle : ObjectProperty X.Modules := fun M =>
  Nonempty (SheafOfModules.FiniteRankVectorBundleData (R := X.ringCatSheaf) M)

/-- The space `|iS_• 𝒫(X)|`, where `𝒫(X)` is the exact category of vector bundles on the scheme
`X` (with exact sequences those that are exact in the abelian category of `𝒪ₓ`-modules). Its
homotopy groups are the algebraic K-groups of `X`: `K_i(X) = π_{i+1} |iS_• 𝒫(X)|` for `i ≥ 0`
([Qu73], §7 and [Wa85], §1.9). -/
noncomputable def algebraicKTheorySpace : TopCat.{u + 1} := kTheorySpace (IsVectorBundle X)

/-- A morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S` is projective if it factors as a closed immersion
`X ⟶ ℙⁿ_S` into a projective space over `S`, followed by the projection `ℙⁿ_S ⟶ S`. -/
def IsProjectiveOver {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (ι : X ⟶ ℙ(Fin (n + 1); S)), IsClosedImmersion ι ∧ (ι ≫ pullback.fst _ _) = f

end Scheme

/-- **Parshin's conjecture.** Let $k$ be a finite field and let $X$ be a smooth projective
variety over $k$ (an integral scheme with a smooth projective structure morphism
$f \colon X \to \operatorname{Spec} k$). Then the higher algebraic K-groups of $X$ vanish up to
torsion: $K_i(X) \otimes \mathbb{Q} = 0$ for all $i > 0$, that is, every element of $K_i(X)$
has finite order.

Here $K_i(X) = \pi_{i+1}(|iS_\bullet \mathcal{P}(X)|, x)$ is the $i$-th algebraic K-group of
the exact category $\mathcal{P}(X)$ of vector bundles on $X$; the space
$|iS_\bullet \mathcal{P}(X)|$ is path-connected, so the statement is the same for every
basepoint $x$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 14 19]
theorem parshins_conjecture (k : Type u) [Field k] [Finite k]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [AlgebraicGeometry.IsIntegral X] (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsSmooth f] (hf : IsProjectiveOver f)
    (i : ℕ) (hi : 0 < i) (x : algebraicKTheorySpace X) :
    Monoid.IsTorsion (π_ (i + 1) (algebraicKTheorySpace X) x) := by
  sorry

end ParshinsConjecture
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot decomposition is appropriate; the article's dim 0 and dim 1 known cases are theorems (Quillen, Harder), not part of the conjecture statement.
modeling_decisions: Higher algebraic K-theory is not in Mathlib. Following Quillen (Higher algebraic K-theory I, §7), K_i(X) is taken to be the K-theory of the exact category 𝒫(X) of vector bundles (locally free 𝒪_X-modules of finite rank), with exact sequences those exact in the abelian category `X.Modules`. The K-theory space is built by Waldhausen's S•-construction rather than Quillen's Q-construction (they are naturally homotopy equivalent for exact categories, Waldhausen 1985 §1.9 / Weibel K-book IV.8); the Q-construction would require iso-classes of spans with a composition law whose well-definedness needs nontrivial proofs. K_i(X) := π_{i+1}|iS_•𝒫(X)| for i ≥ 0.

S_n𝒫 is formalized literally as Waldhausen's category of functors Ar[n] = Arrow (Fin (n+1)) → A with F(i,i) zero, all F(i,j) in P, and F(i,j) → F(i,k) → F(j,k) short exact (`ShortComplex.ShortExact`) for all i ≤ j ≤ k. The zero condition is phrased as `f.left = f.right → IsZero (F.obj f)` (equivalent in a preorder category). Exactness is phrased as `∃ w, (ShortComplex.mk _ _ w).ShortExact` since the composite being zero is automatic (it factors through F(j,j) = 0).

iS_n is `Core` of the full subcategory; the realization of the simplicial category is the geometric realization (`SSet.toTop`) of the diagonal of the bisimplicial nerve. Homotopy groups are Mathlib's `HomotopyGroup.Pi` (`π_`).

Basepoint: the statement quantifies over all basepoints `x : algebraicKTheorySpace X`. The space is path-connected (all vertices are zero functors, all isomorphic through degenerate 1-simplices), so this is equivalent to the statement for K_i(X) at the canonical basepoint; constructing the canonical point in the realization inside Lean was judged not worth the added risk. The space is nonempty (the zero sheaf is a vector bundle of rank 0), so the statement is not vacuous.
'Vanish up to torsion' (K_i(X) ⊗ ℚ = 0) is formalized as `Monoid.IsTorsion` of the (abelian, since i+1 ≥ 2) group π_{i+1}.
'Higher' K-groups: `i : ℕ` with `0 < i` (K_0 is excluded, as in the article's `i > 0`).

'Variety' is read as an integral scheme (`AlgebraicGeometry.IsIntegral X`), the Stacks/Hartshorne convention. The conjecture is insensitive to this choice: for a general smooth projective k-scheme (a finite disjoint union of smooth projective integral schemes) K-theory is the product over components. Reviewers preferring the literature phrasing 'X smooth projective over F_q' may wish to drop this hypothesis; the statement is equivalent either way.

'Projective over k' has no Mathlib definition; `IsProjectiveOver f` says `f` factors as a closed immersion into `ℙ(Fin (n+1); Spec k)` (the repo's `ProjectiveSpace`, i.e. ℙⁿ_k) followed by the projection — Hartshorne's definition, which over an affine base agrees with EGA's.
Smoothness is Mathlib's `IsSmooth f` (locally standard smooth), which is mathematically equivalent to smoothness of the structure morphism.
Finite field: `[Field k] [Finite k]`, with `k : Type u` and `X : Scheme.{u}`.

Vector bundles use the repo's `SheafOfModules.FiniteRankVectorBundleData` (open cover on which M restricts to a free module on a finite index type); `IsVectorBundle M := Nonempty (FiniteRankVectorBundleData M)`.

Note: `FormalConjecturesForMathlib` declares a global notation `f ≫ g` for asymptotics, which clashes with categorical composition inside `∃ (w : … = 0)` and `∧`; the file parenthesizes `(a ≫ b) = c` to force the categorical reading.
